market_holds: Spot 139.17 at 18:08 UTC on 2026-11-23 (Yahoo daily close about 138.1). Front-expiry straddle 9.47%, event-implied move 8.21%. Put skew is 21.7 vol points, so the market is paying up for downside protection. Put/call OI is 0.49 (sealed baseline). The stock is up 11.4% over 20 sessions and 15.1% since the last report (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-16), about 5% below its 52-week high. The run-in tracks oil and the retail tape more than company news. DLTR fell from about 131 to 112 in September while diesel rose from $5.6 to $6.5 (FRED GASDESW). It recovered to 138 as WTI fell from 106 to about 90 in early November, and the sharpest day (+9.6% on 11-04) was a sector-wide rally after Booking and Wayfair reported. Consensus Q3 EPS is $0.88-0.93, just above the middle of the company's $0.80-0.95 guide, which includes about $0.50 of tariff-refund reinvestment. The whisper is $1.06, so the buy side already expects a beat above the top of the guide. Consensus Q3 comp is about 3.4% against a 3-4% guide (UBS note). Revenue consensus is $5.05B, the guide midpoint. FY guide is $7.70-8.05, which implies Q4 EPS of about $2.56 at the midpoint, flat against last year's $2.56. The CFO guided Q4 gross margin down year over year on fuel-driven freight surcharges. Short interest fell from about 15.5M shares in June to 7.8M at the 2026-08-14 settlement (Curved Trading, from FINRA data), so positioning is not crowded short. Of the last 7 prints, 4 went up (median absolute move 6.42%). The Q1 beat-and-raise gained 17.9%. Q2 fell 3.9% despite a large underlying beat, because the Q3 EPS guide sat far below the $1.41 consensus once the refund reinvestment was included.
view: This is a company that guides low and beats. Q1 adjusted EPS of $1.74 beat the top of its $1.45-1.60 guide by $0.14. Q2 underlying EPS of $1.39 (excluding the tariff refund) beat the top of its $1.00-1.15 guide by $0.24. A third beat above the top of the guide is the base case, and the $1.06 whisper says the buy side knows it. The one independent series that may not be fully held is traffic. Placer.ai reports Dollar Tree same-store visits up 4.9% in calendar Q3 (July-September) against 1.2% at Dollar General, in an article dated 2026-11-18. Placer's Q2 rolling figure was +1.4% (per Jefferies, 2026-08-19) when the company reported traffic of +0.4%, so August and September must also have run around +5% on Placer. That points to company traffic of perhaps +3-4% in fiscal Q3, against +0.4% in Q2. A traffic-led comp of 4% or more would beat the 3.4% consensus, which still sits in the middle of the guide. Two things work against it. Ticket growth is slowing (4.5% in Q1, 3.3% in Q2) and the 40th-anniversary $1 promotion holds it back further. And Q3 ran into a fuel shock the August guide did not assume: diesel averaged about $6.2-6.5 against $5.6 at guidance, and gasoline peaked at $4.47 in late September against $3.1 a year earlier. Freight costs went up, and the low-income shopper was squeezed toward low-margin consumables. The deciding line is less Q3 than the FY raise and what it implies for Q4, plus holiday commentary. The Q4 implied by the guide is flat year over year, which is conservative. Diesel is now falling ($5.94 on 11-16) but still above the August level, so the Q4 fuel assumption may get a little worse even as the FY guide rises by roughly the Q3 beat. The likely result is a beat, a raise roughly equal to the beat, and a traffic-led comp at or above the top of the guide. That leans positive, but the stock has run 15% with oil and peers, the buy side expects the beat, and the 13:00 ET window sits in a tape that moved -3.6% and +4.9% on the last two sessions. I lean modestly up and would not bet on it.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the traffic acceleration. Placer's +4.9% calendar-Q3 same-store visits against a stale 3.4% sell-side comp consensus suggests a comp at or above the top of the 3-4% guide, and traffic-led. The run-in that came with lower oil and peer prints does not hold this company's own traffic print. Against that, the $1.06 whisper and the 15% run since the last report show the buy side expects an EPS beat, and the fuel spike during the quarter is a margin headwind the guide did not include. Neither is large enough to call.

recommendation.reason: Dated traffic data (Placer +4.9% same-store visits in calendar Q3) and the company's habit of beating the top of its guide point to a beat and a traffic-led comp at or above 4%. But the buy-side whisper ($1.06) already sits above the top of the guide, and the stock ran 15% into the print with oil and peers. An unassumed fuel shock in Q3 and a fuel-driven Q4 gross margin decline leave the FY raise and Q4 implied as a coin flip. The edge is below the 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 comp of 4.5% or more with traffic of +3% or more, and an FY raise above the Q3 beat (Q4 implied up from about $2.56), would make this a clear up. A Q4 or FY guide held or trimmed on freight and fuel, or holiday-to-date commentary that is cautious, would turn it down.

self_critique: The upside case rests on Placer visits, which overstated company traffic by about 1 point in Q2, and the $1 promotion may offset traffic gains in ticket, so the comp could land at 3.5-4%, which the buy side already expects. Against the lean: the stock is up 15% since the last print, close to its post-earnings high, with a whisper above the top of the guide. The Q2 reaction showed the stock trades on the forward guide, and Q4 now carries a fuel headwind the CFO already flagged. A drop on 'beat but Q4 holds back' is entirely plausible, and the heavy put skew says the market fears it. For the lean: guidance has been conservative three times running and the Q4 implied is flat year over year. These roughly cancel, which is why the number stays near 55-58 and I make no call.
approach_notes: Taking the run-in apart (P6) helped: the move was oil and sector, not company news, and that set the bar. P4 (prove 'priced') pushed me to the Placer data against the stale 3.4% comp consensus, but the $1.06 whisper showed the buy side is ahead of the sell side, so a public whisper can show that 'priced' holds even when consensus is stale.
